newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI asks FTC to draw up gasoline sale guidelines.
newsitem.headline: MITI asks FTC to draw up gasoline sale guidelines.

text.p: The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) has asked Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog to draw up guidelines to prevent further dumping of gasoline products onto the market, a MITI official told reporters on Wednesday.

The MITI official quoted Trade Minister Shinji Sato as telling oil industry officials that the industry itself also needs to make efforts to improve its distribution system in order to prevent such a situation from escalating.

Sato's comments were made during a one-hour meeting this morning between MITI and the oil industry, and were in response to a request by the industry for the government to play a stronger role in overseeing prices.

Japan's oil companies have been suffering sharp falls in their profits, partly because of a price war among gasoline stations that has sent retail prices plunging by about 13 percent over the past two years.
The retail price has been falling in spite of rising yen-denominated crude prices.
